rows.text: Google DeepMind released Genie 4 this week. I need someone to explain what a "generative world model with real-time interactive audio" actually means, because every word in that phrase is doing serious work.

rows.text: Okay, so a world model is a system that generates a simulated environment — not just an image, but a space you can interact with. rows.speaker: ALEX
rows.text: So if a door opens in the simulation, the sound changes with it?

rows.speaker: JAMIE
rows.text: Right. Not a pre-baked sound effect sitting in a file somewhere. Audio synthesis that responds to the visual state as it changes. DeepMind says the latency on that synchronization is lower than previous versions, though they haven't published a specific millisecond figure publicly.

rows.speaker: ALEX
rows.text: "Lower than before" is doing a lot of work there.

rows.speaker: JAMIE
rows.text: It is! But the capability itself — a world where the soundscape tracks the visuals in real time — that's genuinely new. Previous versions were visual only.

rows.text: I want to bring in the infrastructure angle because it's unavoidable. DeepMind confirms this requires specific GPU infrastructure for real-time inference.
